takeaway: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma often presents late, with five-year survival of 2–9% in this review. CA19-9 is not a screening test. Adjuvant gemcitabine and, for fit patients with metastatic disease, FOLFIRINOX improve outcomes against older comparators [1].
clinicalQuestion: What is the prognosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma, and which chemotherapy results does this review cite?
background: The review describes a rising incidence and a cancer often found when it is already advanced [1].
studyDesign: Narrative review of risk, diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes.
setting: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma across resectable and metastatic disease.
intervention: Surgery when resectable, adjuvant gemcitabine, and FOLFIRINOX for metastatic disease in the cited trials.
comparator: Surgery alone in CONKO-001; gemcitabine alone in the Conroy trial.
mainFindings: Five-year survival is given as 2–9%, the worst among cancer sites in the review, and the disease is predicted to become the second leading cause of cancer death in some regions. After successful resection, five-year survival is quoted as 27%. CA19-9 has too low a positive predictive value for screening asymptomatic people and is used to monitor response and recurrence. CONKO-001 compared adjuvant gemcitabine after complete resection with surgery alone: median disease-free survival 13.4 versus 6.7 months, five-year survival 20.7% versus 10.4%, and ten-year survival 12.2% versus 7.7%. In metastatic disease, Conroy and colleagues randomised 171 patients per arm to FOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine. Median overall survival was 11.1 months (95% CI 9.0–13.2) versus 6.8 months (5.5–7.6), hazard ratio 0.57 (95% CI 0.45–0.73; P < 0.001), with more adverse effects on FOLFIRINOX [1].
clinicalMeaning: Do not screen with CA19-9. Offer adjuvant gemcitabine rather than surgery alone, and reserve FOLFIRINOX for patients who can tolerate it [1].
limitations: The review's trial summaries are secondary citations. Regimens newer than the review are not added [1].
bottomLine: Survival is poor. Gemcitabine after resection and FOLFIRINOX in metastatic disease are the gains this review documents [1].
practiceImplication: Quote 11.1 versus 6.8 months only for the metastatic FOLFIRINOX comparison, and mention the extra toxicity [1].
safetyOutcomes: FOLFIRINOX caused more adverse effects than gemcitabine in the cited trial.
trustRationale: Narrative review that reports named trial results; it is not itself the trial publication.
whatNotToOverclaim: Do not apply the metastatic FOLFIRINOX result to adjuvant treatment.
